blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A planner models how many transformers to order: none at all, or any number from 6 to 20, because the supplier's minimum order is 6. Which CP-SAT variable states that?

options.text: `new_int_var(0, 20)`, with the solver leaving out 1 to 5 by itself
options.says: A variable may take every value of its domain; 0..20 includes 1 to 5, and nothing in the model removes them.
Right: a domain can be any finite set of integers, such as 'nothing, or at least 6', given as intervals.

options.text: `new_int_var(6, 20)`, with an order of 0 left to the solver
options.says: A domain of 6..20 forbids ordering nothing, which the planner allows.

options.text: a continuous variable over [0, 20], rounded to 0 or to 6 to 20 after the solve
options.says: CP-SAT has no continuous variable: every variable is an integer with a finite domain.

origin.section: Every Variable Is an Integer With a Finite Domain

questions.stem: A crew row puts 1.5, 2 and 2.5 crew-months on three Booleans a, b and c, with a limit of 6. A developer writes `model.add(1.5 * a + 2 * b + 2.5 * c <= 6)`. What happens?

options.text: CP-SAT rounds every coefficient and solves the rounded row
options.says: Nothing is rounded: the row is refused when it is built.

options.text: The solve returns MODEL_INVALID, and validate() names the row
options.says: The refusal comes earlier, in Python, so there is no solve to return a status.

options.text: CP-SAT keeps the fractions and checks the row within a tolerance
options.says: CP-SAT has no tolerance; a row with a fractional coefficient is not accepted at all.

options.text: Python raises a TypeError as the row is built, before a solve
options.says: Right: linear constraints accept only integer coefficients and bounds, and the check happens in `add`.

origin.section: A Linear Constraint Has Whole-Number Coefficients

questions.stem: A nightly job solves a selection model with a time limit. The status comes back FEASIBLE, with objective 9,120 and best objective bound 9,400 (maximizing). What can the job report?

options.text: A plan worth 9,120 exists; no plan is worth more than 9,400
options.says: Right: FEASIBLE carries a plan that was not proved best; the bound caps what any plan can be worth.

options.text: The plan worth 9,120 is the best one, and 9,400 is out of reach
options.says: That is OPTIMAL. FEASIBLE means the search stopped before proving the plan best.

options.text: No plan can be read at all, so 9,120 and 9,400 are only estimates
options.says: FEASIBLE is one of the two statuses that carry a plan; UNKNOWN is the one with none.

options.text: The model breaks a rule of CP-SAT, so 9,120 and 9,400 mean nothing
options.says: That is MODEL_INVALID, a refusal before any search, with no objective to report.

origin.section: Read the Status Before You Read a Value
